text: Answering the client first: on Zerodha, buying Reliance (around Rs 3,000 a share, so Rs 10,000 buys 3 shares) as delivery costs about 0.38% round-trip all-in, roughly Rs 38 on Rs 10,000, with the flat Rs 15.93 DP charge on sale being the sneaky part. On IPOs: Indian IPO minimum lots are usually Rs 14,000-15,000, so Rs 10,000 typically can't even apply, and US IPOs aren't open to small retail at issue price. On the spotlight, HONASA's fundamentals genuinely impress me: revenue up 27% YoY, operating margin expanded from 5.9% to 13.2% in five quarters, and six straight earnings beats averaging 30%+ surprises, which explains the 67.5% one-year CAGR. But a -62.9% max drawdown and 2024's -42.1% year say this stock can halve on you, so it's a position-size candidate, not a 10x vehicle.
